title: Outlook 2027
summary: After an energy shock and the impacts of AI rocked financial markets in 2026, what lies ahead in 2027?

# Outlook 2027


## Until the music stops


16 November 2026


**Share this Insight**


Share page via Facebook


Share page via X


Share page via LinkedIn


Share page via email


Welcome to our Outlook 2027, as our Chief Investment Office at Barclays Private Bank and Wealth Management dissect the last year and examine what it might mean for investors.


It’s been a challenging year for financial markets. An energy shock revived inflation and led the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates for the first time in three years. Long-term borrowing costs climbed to their highest in more than two decades. Yet equities reached new records, carried by the extraordinary earnings of companies at the heart of artificial intelligence (AI).


Our Outlook explores how these forces have played out across the largest economies and what they mean for bonds, equities and alternatives strategies. Higher yields have created a more supportive backdrop for income investors, even if fiscal strains suggest caution. In equities, we expect earnings rather than valuations to set the pace, with leadership likely to remain heavily AI-dependent.


No one knows when the music will stop. That is why we spend as much time on how portfolios are built as where the opportunities lie. When one theme runs through so much of the market, diversifying by what drives returns, not by asset class labels, matters more. The year ahead calls for agility and composure, and our teams see ample opportunities for investors prepared to stay disciplined.


As always, we hope you enjoy the articles, and we thank you for entrusting us with your investments.


**Jean-Damien Marie Global Head of Investments, Private Bank and Wealth Management**
